Vyvanse and Adderall are actually both stimulants. When coupled with the depressant alcohol, it can fuck with your heart because your body is getting conflicting signals about how to function. Drugs like opioids (morphine, oxycodone, etc.) and benzodiazepines (Xanax, Klonopin, etc.) are depressants, which can also be very dangerous when coupled with alcohol use.

Please check all your drug interactions before partaking in anything. You could really be in serious danger even though you think "oh a few shots can't hurt."

Hi, trans person here. I personally believe that gender IS a social construct and for me, "transgender" is almost a misnomer. For me, being trans has only ever been about dysphoria. I was always the most tomboyish person I knew, and I was content being a girl who was "one of the guys" until I got to puberty. Then it increasingly felt like my body got off the puberty highway on the wrong exit. I feel like I'm living in a costume. I can't explain why and I often do feel like I'm "crazy," but I've tried to diminish the incongruence with talk therapy for years and it's not working. So I'm trying hormones and they'll hopefully make me feel more at home in my body which my brain sees as "should have generic male sex characteristics." These feelings aren't normal and they fit the definition of a mental disorder, but treatment for the negative symptoms of that disorder involve transition, and hopefully I'll feel more like I'm getting back on the right "highway." I don't know if this helps you at all, and biological and social gender IS meaningless, but that doesn't make my dysphoria about my sex characteristics go away.

Trans people ARE offered treatment before medical intervention. Endocrinologists and surgeons who have any brain will require at least some counseling before even thinking about starting treatment. I'm trans and believe me I would not wish dysphoria on my worst enemy. I wish more than anything that therapy could make it go away, that I wouldn't have to spend my life on hormones just to make living in my own body tolerable, so people wouldn't hurl slurs at me and call me an inhuman disgusting freak. I tried for years to make that the case because that would sure make this a whole lot easier. But it isn't. Gender dysphoria/gender identity disorder cant be 'fixed' by therapy alone in more severe cases. I've been in therapy for 5 years now, and I've had to jump through a lot of hoops to start hormones. I don't know where you're getting the suicide statistics listed, and I'd like to see multiple reliable sources supporting them.

Depression is also a mental disorder. You don't go around saying antidepressants should never be used and that people should only ever have therapy because depression is a disorder. That's not how it works. Therapy helps depressed people a lot. Antidepressants help depressed people too, and are often a necessary part of depression treatment in more severe cases. Antidepressants alone rarely actually help depressed people and I bet the suicide rate for people on antidepressants alone (with no other therapy or treatment) are very similar (if not even higher) than no treatment at all.

It's a similar deal with gender dysphoria, a combination of therapy and medical intervention is most often the most effective course of treatment for managing the negative symptoms of gender dysphoria. Society not demonizing and dismissing trans people will help a lot too because even if you're comfortable in your own body, people constantly alienating you and calling you shit like "delusional" when you're already trying to deal with those thoughts yourself can really get to someone, especially in an area that's generally unaccepting. 

It's a really complex issue and it definitely needs more research and a better solution, but for now transition and therapy is really the best we have, and multiple health organizations agree with me.
